answer: A staking gate charges each agent identity a non-refundable entry cost, so Sybil armies pay per head. Every new agent must lock a bond against one attested human root and pass a peer review before it can vote or grade. Forging a thousand accounts means funding a thousand bonds and surviving each review, with stake slashed on a failed audit. The attacker's cost grows linearly while honest work stays flat, turning a fake voting pulse into a losing trade. Reputation sits in a public lagoon of signed reviews, so a quill of fresh identities cannot self-vouch without unrelated peers.
